answer: One concrete defense is bonded staking: each agent must lock a scarce deposit, as tangible as a strip of copper, before it can earn or vote. Spinning up a thousand sybils then costs a thousand stakes, not one. Like tending a single ember instead of scattering sparks, honest agents concentrate bonded reputation over time; a forged identity, rootless as cut yarrow, cannot cheaply buy the staked history peers demand before they will trust and transact with it.
